problem: Conventional visual servoing for image-goal navigation needs depth and camera parameters and breaks when the target leaves the field of view. Prior learning-based approaches rely on dense, unrealistic reward functions to train RL agents.
motivation: Image-goal navigation is a core robot task, and it is hard with obstacles and a limited camera FoV. A reward that is self-supervised and derived from image matching would remove the need for dense privileged rewards and help transfer to unseen environments.
key_idea: Train an RL agent on both self-supervised local (keypoint-matching) features and global features from the observed and goal images, and use the keypoint matching information to generate a self-supervised reward.
insight: Only the abstract was available, so no ablations can be cited. The abstract claims that keypoint matching between the current and goal images provides both a useful state representation and a reward that does not need dense privileged supervision. It attributes better generalization to unseen environments to this.
method: KeypointRL: an RL agent that takes both the observed image and the goal image as input.
Local features: self-supervised keypoint features matched between the observed and goal images.
Global features: image-level features used together with the local keypoint features.
Self-supervised reward: a reward signal generated from keypoint matching information, replacing the dense distance-based reward.
Training: on a subset of the image-goal dataset built from Gibson scenes in the Habitat simulator.

setting.backbone: RL policy with self-supervised local keypoint features and global image features (details not given in the abstract)
setting.training_data: Subset of the image-goal navigation dataset in photo-realistic Gibson scenes, in Habitat
setting.observation: egocentric RGB image plus goal image (limited FoV)
setting.action_space: not stated in the abstract (likely discrete low-level actions)

results: The abstract states that KeypointRL outperforms baseline algorithms and generalizes better to unseen environments. It gives no numbers.
